question: What main condition is methyldopa used to manage in pregnant women?
explanation: Methyldopa is a first-line medication used to manage high blood pressure conditions like chronic or gestational hypertension during pregnancy. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why is methyldopa often chosen over other blood pressure drugs in pregnancy?

options.A: It has a long safety record for use during pregnancy
options.B: It requires only a single dose taken just before delivery
options.C: It completely cures chronic hypertension within the first trimester
options.D: It completely prevents the development of pre-eclampsia

explanation: Decades of clinical use provide reassuring safety data regarding fetal development, making clinicians confident in prescribing it to expectant mothers. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h1)

question: Which specific receptors does methyldopa stimulate in the brainstem?
explanation: Methyldopa works centrally by stimulating alpha-2 adrenergic receptors, which lowers activity in the sympathetic nervous system. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h2)

question: How does lowering sympathetic nervous system activity help reduce blood pressure?

options.A: By increasing the total volume of circulating blood
options.C: By increasing the resting heart rate significantly
options.D: By blocking sodium retention in the renal tubules

explanation: Reducing sympathetic tone relaxes blood vessels throughout the body, lowering the resistance against which the heart pumps and thereby reducing blood pressure. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h2)

question: At what blood pressure reading is medication usually started during pregnancy?
explanation: Blood pressure readings consistently exceeding 140 over 90 mmHg generally prompt the start of blood pressure treatment in pregnant women. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h3)

question: A pregnant woman at 28 weeks presents with chronic high blood pressure. Which drug is a standard first-line choice?
explanation: Methyldopa is a standard first-line oral medication for managing chronic hypertension in pregnant women due to its safety profile. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is a typical starting dose for oral methyldopa therapy in pregnancy?
explanation: Starting at 250 milligrams two to three times daily helps the patient tolerate the medication and minimizes side effects like drowsiness. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why is the dose of methyldopa increased gradually over several days?

options.A: To allow time for blood pressure to stabilize and minimize sudden side effects
options.B: To bypass the need for regular antenatal blood pressure checks
options.C: To prevent the drug from accumulating in the amniotic fluid immediately
options.D: To ensure the placenta absorbs all active metabolites all at once

explanation: Gradual titration prevents abrupt drops in blood pressure and helps the patient adjust to side effects like drowsiness. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common side effect of methyldopa?
explanation: Hair loss is not a recognized side effect of methyldopa, whereas sedation, dry mouth, and dizziness are common. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why is periodic liver function testing recommended for patients taking methyldopa long-term?

options.A: To screen for gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: To measure how fast the kidneys filter out excess protein
options.C: To detect rare drug-induced liver injury or enzyme elevations
options.D: To calculate the exact gestational age of the fetus

explanation: Although rare, methyldopa can cause liver irritation, making periodic liver enzyme checks a safe practice during prolonged use. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h5)

question: What common side effect should a midwife warn a patient to expect during the first few days of taking methyldopa?
explanation: Sedation and drowsiness are very common when first starting methyldopa or increasing the dose. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why must a midwife advise a patient never to stop taking methyldopa suddenly?

options.A: Stopping suddenly can cause a dangerous rebound spike in blood pressure
options.B: It causes permanent damage to maternal heart valves
options.C: It will immediately trigger preterm labor contractions
options.D: It leads to instant fetal growth restriction

explanation: Abrupt discontinuation of this medication can result in rebound hypertension, putting the mother at risk. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h6)
